title: App sign-in with unsaved changes
summary: Diceroll's App sign-in with two edits waiting for Save: Apple turned off by the operator (the row says 'Not saved' with 'Use the default', and a caution about App Store guideline 4.8) and Email moved from Optional to Required, which takes the value over from the manifest. The SaveBar names both changes and says players are asked again.
compare: Save model: Sign-in methods, What Diceroll gets, License keys and Customer portal are one resource (the product's sign-in settings), so their controls only mark the page dirty and one SaveBar lists every change by section. The Status switch is the Sign-in feature and applies on its own (turning it off asks first: identity.sign-in-off). The product connection is edited in its own dialog from 'Edit'. 'Inside the game' rows have no control.

A changed row carries an accent bar at its leading edge and 'Not saved' under its text; the rail puts a dot after each section with changes. Leaving the page with changes asks first (useUnsavedChangesGuard).
An overridden derived provider reads 'Not saved' with 'Use the default'; after Save the row keeps 'Use the default'. No reason line: the switch shows the state.

Turning Apple off for a product that ships on iOS while Google or Steam stays on shows the caution under the row at once, before Save, citing App Store Review Guideline 4.8. It is a caution, not a block: Save stays available.

A value set by identity.claims in .pkey/product says it was taken from the manifest ('Not saved · was Optional'), with the consequence on its own line ('Players who didn’t share it must share it to continue'); after Save its section shows 'Changed here' and 'Revert to manifest…', as License keys does on identity.app-sign-in.

The SaveBar sticks to the bottom of the window under the cards column (a mockup draws it where it rests, at the end of the page): the count, each change in words ('Apple off; Email required'), 'Discard' and 'Save 2 changes'. Saving shows 'Saving…' and then the toast 'Saved 2 changes to App sign-in'.
Phone: the caution spans the card under the row, and the SaveBar's buttons share its last row.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Masthead mark (B4): from 1024px a 48px flat tile on this page (the feature's glyph on a landing page, the product's icon on a product page) replaces the orientation chip; below 1024 the chip carries the context; never on a dense data page, a record or a state page.
Round 2 (UX review): Changed rows are an ink bar and wash with 'Not saved' in strong text; the save bar is neutral (B2).
B17: License for this device and License keys are license, the Cloud Sync row sync, Customer portal and Presentation core; the rest identity.

findings.issue: Spacing scale inconsistent (16, 24 and 32 used at random); card header heights and title sizes vary.
findings.resolution: Opt-in .rhythm on the page: 24 between cards in a group, 12 group title to first card, 32 between groups; card header at least 56; card titles 18/600; stat tiles 24. The global tokens are unchanged (existing values); muted and meta text already met 4.5:1 and 12px.
Rebuilt on the same two-column layout and copy.

findings.issue: Save bar wrapped to 4 or 5 lines on phone (about 130px).
findings.resolution: One line '2 changes: Apple off, Email required'; Discard and Save share a row; the 39% consequence moved into the Email row's 'Not saved' note; Apple row subtitle 'Off by you'.
